newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land dips, expected to rise later.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land dips, expected to rise later.

text.p: DBS Land Ltd shares dipped on Wednesday after trading in the stock resumed after a suspension to announce a share placement to raise funds, but dealers said they thought the fall was temporary.
"The initial impact has been a dip, but I think later it will take off again," a dealer at a local firm said.
DBS Land said on Tuesday it would issue 92 million new shares to raise Singapore $427 million to "partially finance and refinance its purchase of shares of Parkway Holdings".
DBS Land took a 19 percent stake in healthcare group Parkway in May and the market has been expecting a bid for a further stake or a full takeover to follow.
The shares were placed at S$4.75 each, a 25-cent discount on Monday's closing value before the one-day suspension and slightly below dealers estimates of where the shares should be trading.
"I thought about $4.80 to S$4.85 would have been fair," one dealer said.
At 0125, GMT DBS Land shares stood down Singapore $0.16 at S$4.84 on volume of 68,500 units.
Parkway shares were unchanged at S$7.00, but Parkway warrants were up S$0.10 at S$5.10.
